question: What was the main objection against the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constituent Assembly?

options.text: They were considered as novel features
They were non justiciable in character
They were an instrument of instructions
The state was responsible for these policies

solution:
The correct answer is __**They were non justiciable in character**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy** were criticized in the Constituent Assembly for being **non-justiciable in character**.
 
• Being non-justiciable means that these principles cannot be enforced by any court of law.
 
• Despite their non-justiciable nature, they are **fundamental in the governance of the country** and aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They are intended to guide the state in the application of laws and policies, aiming at achieving social and economic democracy.
 
• The Directive Principles are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution and include guidelines for the creation of a welfare state, aiming at reducing income inequality, ensuring fair distribution of wealth, and securing a decent standard of living for all citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constituent Assembly** was established to draft the Constitution of India and held its first session on **9th December 1946**.
 
• The Assembly included representatives from various regions and communities of India, ensuring a comprehensive and inclusive approach to the drafting process.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, known as the principal architect of the Indian Constitution, chaired the Drafting Committee.
 
• The Directive Principles were inspired by the Irish Constitution and aim to establish a just society in India.
 
• While they are not enforceable by courts, they are considered essential for the governance of the country and aim to create a framework for a welfare state.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made to address evolving needs and circumstances, as outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The principles emphasize goals such as securing an adequate means of livelihood, equitable distribution of resources, health and education, and protection of the environment.
